authority: Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park Authority
researched_by: the Authority's own byelaw pages and booking system, plus an Argyll and Bute FOI response
policy_summary:
Camping Management Byelaws, in force 1 March to 30 September each year across Camping Management Zones covering less than 4% of the park's 720 square miles. Introduced 2017 with a ten-year review, which is live now - public consultation runs to 21 September 2026, and motorhome rules are one of the five things being reviewed.

Sleeping in a vehicle inside a zone without a permit is an OFFENCE. Permits are GBP4.30 per night for a tent or a motorhome alike, valid 19:00 to 10:00 for vehicles, bookable up to three nights and four weeks ahead. Breach is reported to the Procurator Fiscal, with a fine of up to GBP500 - the only criminal penalty with a stated figure anywhere in this dataset.

Outside the zones, and across the whole park from October to February, the byelaws do not apply.
notes:
THE CARVE-OUT IS THE MOST USEFUL FACT IN THIS DATASET FOR SCOTLAND.

The byelaw makes it an offence to sleep in a vehicle in a Camping Management Zone WITHOUT A PERMIT - unless the vehicle is on a road, which includes a lay-by, as defined by the Roads (Scotland) Act 1984. And the byelaws do not apply at all to lay-bys controlled by Transport Scotland on trunk roads inside the zones.

So a van in a lay-by inside a zone is lawful without a permit. The same van parked ten metres off the road on the lochshore is committing an offence. The line is the road, not the zone.

Argyll and Bute confirmed by FOI that there are no clearways on their roads within the West Loch Lomond zone and nothing prohibiting overnight camping in their lay-bys, and that three of their off-street car parks sit inside the zone. The limit is road traffic law rather than the byelaw: permanent encampment on a road is a separate offence.

Second point people get wrong. The Scottish Outdoor Access Code gives a right to wild camp - and it EXCLUDES motor vehicles. There is no van equivalent of Scotland's wild camping right anywhere, in or out of a national park.

ADDENDUM 27 July 2026 - OWN-PROVISION SWEEP (step 2 of the protocol).

The Authority does not only regulate camping here, it SELLS it, and the two halves of its own website do not talk to each other. Three findings.

FIRST, THE MOTORHOME PERMIT AREAS NOW HAVE NAMES. The open question above - which permit areas take motorhomes - is answered on the motorhomes page, not the permit page: Firkin Point and Inveruglas on the west shore of Loch Lomond, and Three Lochs Forest Drive north of Aberfoyle. Three areas out of the whole permit network. That is the single most useful sentence the Authority publishes about vans and it appears nowhere near the byelaw pages.

SECOND, THE PRICE HAS MOVED AND THE VEHICLE TERMS ARE DIFFERENT FROM THE TENT TERMS. A permit is now GBP4.50 a night, not GBP4.30. A tent permit runs from 13:00; a MOTORHOME permit is valid only 19:00 to 10:00, so the vehicle may not sit there in daylight. Bays are capped at 8m by 2.5m, which excludes a lot of A-class and large coachbuilts. And there is a return gap the tent rules do not have: nobody in the party may take another permit in the SAME area within three nights of the last one expiring. Three Lochs Forest Drive also charges GBP3 vehicle access on top, and its barrier is locked at 16:00 in and 17:00 out, which has to be reconciled with a 19:00 permit start - unresolved, and logged below.

THIRD, AND COUNTERINTUITIVELY: THE AUTHORITY RUNS FOUR CAMPSITES AND NONE OF THEM TAKES A VAN. Loch Chon and Loch Achray were built as part of the byelaw scheme, Sallochy is on the east shore and Inchcailloch is an island. Each campsite page carries the same flat sentence - 'there are no motorhome/campervan spaces at X campsite'. The motorhomes page, meanwhile, lists all four under a heading that reads as though they take motorhomes. They do not. A van arriving at Loch Chon on the strength of that page has nowhere to go.

So the Authority's van offer is three permit bays-areas and a free waste point at Tarbet, and its campsite estate is closed to vehicles. Inchcailloch is boat access only and is not recorded as a site here for that reason. Coilessan, described as closed for the season, is a permit area in the Argyll Forest Park rather than one of the four campsites, and is not recorded because its status could not be pinned down.
open_questions: Price discrepancy: the Authority's pages say GBP4.30, one secondary source says GBP4.50. Check at booking.
WHICH permit areas accept motorhomes? The Authority says 'some locations' without a list - that is the gap that matters most.
What does the 2026 review conclude? Consultation closes 21 September 2026 and motorhome rules are in scope, so this record has a known expiry.
Which lay-bys inside the zones are Transport Scotland's and which are council-controlled? The distinction decides lawfulness and nobody publishes a map.

RESOLVED 27 July 2026: the motorhome permit areas are Firkin Point, Inveruglas and Three Lochs Forest Drive. Price is now GBP4.50, not GBP4.30. The two questions above are answered; left in place because they show what was unknown before the own-provision sweep.

Three Lochs Forest Drive locks its entrance barrier at 16:00 and its exit barrier at 17:00, but a motorhome permit does not start until 19:00. How does a permit holder get in? Either the barrier times differ for permit holders or the drive is left open - the Authority publishes neither.

How many motorhome bays are there at Firkin Point and at Inveruglas? The Authority publishes no count for any permit area, so the total size of the legal overnight van offer inside the zones is unknown.
Coilessan: the motorhomes page says it is 'closed for the season' but it is not one of the four listed campsites. Is it a permit area in the Argyll Forest Park, and does it take vehicles?
Sallochy campsite is described as temporarily closed on one Authority page and open for bookings on another, on the same day. Which is right?

sites.name: Camping Management Zone permit areas (motorhome permits, where available)
sites.notes: GBP4.30 a night, the same as a tent, and the cheapest legitimate overnight anywhere in this dataset. Valid 19:00 to 10:00. No formal facilities - these are permitted wild camping spots, not aires. Only SOME permit areas accept motorhomes and the Authority does not list which.

sites.name: Lay-bys and roads inside the Camping Management Zones
sites.notes: LAWFUL WITHOUT A PERMIT. The byelaw exempts vehicles on a road, which includes lay-bys, as defined by the Roads (Scotland) Act 1984, and does not apply at all to Transport Scotland lay-bys on trunk roads. You may stop and rest, including sleeping overnight. Permanent encampment on a road remains an offence under road traffic law, so this is for a night, not a week.

sites.name: Camping Management Zones, off the road, without a permit
sites.notes: An offence to sleep in a vehicle inside a zone without a permit, unless on a road. Reported to the Procurator Fiscal with a fine of up to GBP500 - a criminal matter, not a parking ticket. Zones run from the lochshore to the nearby road and about 200m beyond it, or to the nearest visible feature. Seasonal: 1 March to 30 September only.

sites.name: The rest of the National Park, and everywhere October to February
sites.notes: The byelaws cover under 4% of 720 square miles. Outside the zones, and across the whole park from October to February, they do not apply - though the Scottish Outdoor Access Code that governs instead explicitly excludes motor vehicles, so there is still no positive right to sleep in a van. Parking law applies.

sites.name: Firkin Point motorhome permit area, west Loch Lomond
sites.search_hint: Firkin Point picnic area, old A82 loop, west shore of Loch Lomond between Tarbet and Inveruglas
sites.notes: One of only three permit areas in the whole park that accepts a motorhome or campervan. GBP4.50 a night, valid 19:00 to 10:00 only - the vehicle cannot sit here through the day. Bay limit 8m by 2.5m. Nobody in the party may take another permit in this same area within three nights of the last one expiring. Season 1 March to 30 September; outside that the byelaws do not apply and no permit is sold. No facilities: no water, no waste, no toilets. The nearest waste disposal is the free point at Tarbet, about 5km north.
sites.geocode_precision: Firkin Point headland and the old-road picnic loop off the A82

sites.name: Inveruglas motorhome permit area, west Loch Lomond
sites.search_hint: Inveruglas visitor centre and An Ceann Mor viewpoint car park, A82 north Loch Lomond, opposite Sloy power station
sites.notes: The northernmost of the three motorhome permit areas, on the A82 by the Inveruglas visitor centre and the An Ceann Mor viewpoint. Same terms as Firkin Point: GBP4.50, 19:00 to 10:00, three nights maximum, three-night gap before returning to the same area, 8m by 2.5m bay limit, 1 March to 30 September. Cafe and toilets at the visitor centre in season but nothing overnight - treat it as a bay, not an aire.
sites.geocode_precision: Inveruglas hamlet and the A82 lochside visitor centre area

sites.name: Three Lochs Forest Drive motorhome permit area, north of Aberfoyle
sites.price_note: GBP4.50 permit plus a GBP3 vehicle access charge for the forest drive itself
payment_methods: coins and card at the drive barrier
sites.search_hint: Three Lochs Forest Drive entrance, A821 about two miles north of Aberfoyle, FK8 3SY
sites.notes: The only inland motorhome permit area, and the awkward one. The drive is Forestry and Land Scotland land inside Queen Elizabeth Forest Park, but the overnight permits are the National Park Authority's and are bought from the Authority - so it belongs here, with FLS named as the landowner. Two charges apply: GBP3 to bring a vehicle onto the drive, GBP4.50 for the permit. Drive open Easter to October from 09:00, entrance barrier locked 16:00 and exit barrier 17:00, which is hard to square with a permit that only starts at 19:00 - see open questions. Coordinate is the barrier at the A821 entrance, not a bay; the permit bays are spread along the drive.
sites.geocode_precision: entrance barrier to the forest drive off the A821, from the Authority's own grid reference NN 517 036

sites.name: Loch Chon Campsite (National Park Authority)
sites.price_note: GBP11.20 per adult per night, GBP2.20 per child aged 5-15, GBP3.30 per vehicle for the one designated space per booking; free arriving on foot or by bicycle
prohibits: no bins - take all waste away
sites.search_hint: Loch Chon Campsite, B829 between Aberfoyle and Inversnaid, FK8 3TL
sites.notes: Built by the Authority as part of the 2017 camping byelaw scheme and run by it directly - this is the Authority's own provision, not a permit area. 26 tent pitches, two accessible, one double. AND IT TAKES NO VEHICLES: 'there are no motorhome/campervan spaces at Loch Chon campsite'. The GBP3.30 vehicle charge buys a parking space for a car, not a pitch for a van. Open year round, bookable four weeks ahead, three nights maximum. No showers, no bins, no phone signal, heavy midges in summer. About 6.9 miles from Aberfoyle on the B829.
sites.geocode_precision: the campsite at the south end of Loch Chon on the B829

sites.name: Loch Achray Campsite (National Park Authority)
sites.price_note: GBP11.20 per adult per night, GBP2.20 per child aged 5-15, GBP3.30 per vehicle for the one designated space per booking
facilities: accessible pitches 16 and 17 with accessible toilets
prohibits: no bins - take all waste away
sites.search_hint: Loch Achray Campsite, Three Lochs Forest Drive, Trossachs, six miles west of Callander
sites.notes: The second campsite built under the byelaw scheme and run by the Authority. 17 tent pitches in open and woodland areas. Same flat exclusion as Loch Chon: 'there are no motorhome/campervan spaces at Loch Achray Campsite'. Open year round, four weeks ahead, three nights maximum, no showers, no bins. Reached through the Three Lochs Forest Drive from Aberfoyle or from the Callander side - which means a van can buy a permit on the drive it drives past this campsite on, but cannot pitch at the campsite.
sites.geocode_precision: the campsite between Loch Achray and Loch Venachar, near Achray church

sites.name: Sallochy Campsite (National Park Authority)
sites.price_note: GBP11.20 per adult per night, GBP2.20 per child aged 5-15, GBP3.30 per vehicle for the one designated space per booking
sites.search_hint: Sallochy campsite, east Loch Lomond shore road near Rowardennan, about 9 miles from Drymen
sites.notes: Woodland tent pitches on the east shore of Loch Lomond by the West Highland Way, run by the Authority. Not a byelaw-era build - this one predates the others and sits on ground long associated with Forestry and Land Scotland, which is why FLS still appears against it in some listings; the Authority's own campsite page presents it as one of its four. No motorhome or campervan spaces. Status contradictory: the find-a-campsite index says 'Sallochy Bay campsite is temporarily closed' while the site's own page says it is open for bookings. Coordinate is the Sallochy locality on the shore road and is corroborated by only one source, so treat it as approximate.
sites.geocode_precision: Sallochy locality on the east Loch Lomond shore road; the campsite is at Sallochy Bay, single-source and not corroborated
